Scion Asset Management, led by famed investor Michael Burry, has disclosed **[bearish put options on Nvidia and Palantir](https://substack.com/redirect/006d7bb7-cb3d-4ffb-9aca-bd086e028f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in his 13F filings on Monday, echoing his "Big Short" prescience amid AI bubble warnings and cryptic social media hints of market froth.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/006d7bb7-cb3d-4ffb-9aca-bd086e028f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bulls Eye Energy Pharma** : Burry countered his bearish AI wagers with bullish call options on oilfield giant Halliburton and drugmaker Pfizer, signaling bets on undervalued sectors amid tech turbulence.
* **Second Nvidia Short Strike** : Following Q1's aggressive puts on Nvidia and Chinese tech firms, Burry liquidated most equities and doubled down, eyeing potential AI overvaluation collapse.
* **Palantir Valuation Sparks Selloff** : Shares plunged over 10% post-disclosure as analysts flagged Palantir's valuation, despite upbeat revenue guidance, which drew increased short-seller scrutiny.
* **Circular AI Deals Alarms** : Burry amplified concerns via X posts on opaque financing loops involving Nvidia, OpenAI, and peers, hinting at artificial hype inflating the sector's boom.

Palantir Technologies' **[shares plunged](https://substack.com/redirect/c615cead-a237-4565-bfc4-cbadcea28a84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as much as 10% Tuesday despite blockbuster Q3 results and Q4 guidance topping Wall Street forecasts, as analysts slammed the stock's sky-high 230x price-to-earnings ratio amid fading AI hype fears.
* **Q3 Revenue Surges Wildly** : Total revenue hit $1.18 billion, up 63% year-over-year and beating $1.09 billion estimates, fueled by explosive U.S. commercial growth.
* **US Commercial Boom Accelerates** : Commercial revenue soared 121% to $397 million, exceeding $342 million expectations, signaling robust private-sector AI adoption.
* **Guidance Raised Amid Headwinds** : Full-year outlook boosted to $4.4 billion from $4.15 billion, even as U.S. government shutdown risks loom over federal contracts.

* * *
* * *
# Bitcoin breaks below $100,000 benchmark in Crypto sell off
In a stark reversal of crypto's bullish streak, **[Bitcoin tumbled 6%](https://substack.com/redirect/b497e791-8e73-4ce4-a1e1-50bb009f7855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to $99,994 today, intensifying its November sell-off as jittery investors dumped risk assets amid mounting doubts over the AI boom's sustainability--echoing a 37% plunge from a similar slump in 2018.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b497e791-8e73-4ce4-a1e1-50bb009f7855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **November Volatility Echoes History** : Bitcoin's failure to gain from October's traditional seasonal boost marks the first such miss since 2018, when it cratered 37% the following month, signaling potential for sharper declines ahead.
* **Ether Joins Crypto Rout** : The second-largest cryptocurrency by market cap, Ether, plunged over 11% in two days to $3,255, mirroring Bitcoin's woes as shared investors flee high-valuation AI stocks like Palantir despite its robust earnings.
* **Long-Term Holders Drive Pressure** : Sustained selling by veteran crypto investors has persisted in this bull market, with reduced retail buying compared to past cycles heightening risks of further drops if newer holders panic-sell.
* **Support Levels Loom Large** : Analysts see $100,000 as a critical threshold for Bitcoin, with deeper backing above $95,000, but warn of scant near-term catalysts to halt the risk-off spiral tied to Nasdaq's 1.75% dip.

* * *
* * *
# Hollywood star reveals that backlash over Kirk murder nearly broke her
Former "Wicked" Broadway star Kristin Chenoweth revealed in a Hollywood Reporter interview that **[vicious online backlash from fans](https://substack.com/redirect/a1066938-4d74-4fb4-953b-231292d09c68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** accusing her of betraying the LGBTQ+ community after a sympathetic post about assassinated conservative activist Charlie Kirk's death in September left her emotionally shattered, nearly breaking her spirit despite her unyielding faith and advocacy.
* **Chenoweth 's Heartfelt Post Exposed**: Chenoweth shared Instagram grief over Kirk's young family and heavenly peace, despite ideological clashes, which sparked the immediate fury from fans.
* **Faith-Advocacy Clash Intensifies** : As a devout Christian and LGBTQ+ champion, Chenoweth defended her "human moment" of reflection, insisting her beliefs harmonize without contradiction.
* **Curtis Echoes Similar Storm** : Jamie Lee Curtis faced parallel outrage for tearful faith remarks on Kirk, later clarifying a "mistranslation" that twisted her intent into undue positivity.
* **Personal Toll Demands Silence** : Chenoweth admitted that the vitriol "hurt me so badly," Chenoweth has refused further discussion on the issue, declaring she's privately healed from the ordeal's depths.

# **Vice President Cheney dead at 84 leaving a contentious legacy**
Former U.S. Vice President Dick Cheney, the hawkish architect of the Iraq War under George W. Bush, **[died Monday at 84](https://substack.com/redirect/d5fdb61f-166c-4f41-9d43-65c926053296?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from pneumonia and heart complications, leaving a polarizing legacy of power, controversy that reshaped American foreign policy in a post 9/11 world.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d5fdb61f-166c-4f41-9d43-65c926053296?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Iraq War Advocate** : Cheney fiercely championed the 2003 invasion of Iraq, falsely linking Saddam Hussein to 9/11 and al Qaeda, insisting U.S. troops would be "greeted as liberators" leading to a decade-long quagmire.
* **Heart Transplant Survivor** : Plagued by lifelong cardiac issues since his first heart attack at 37, Cheney underwent a life-saving heart transplant in 2012, enabling his continued public defense of controversial policies like "enhanced interrogation" techniques labeled as torture.
* **Halliburton CEO Tenure** : From 1995 to 2000, he led the oil services giant Halliburton, securing a $35 million retirement package amid scrutiny over its lucrative Iraq War contracts, fueling accusations of war profiteering tied to his administration role.
* **Trump Foe Endgame** : In a stunning break from GOP norms, Cheney branded Donald Trump the "greatest threat" to the republic and endorsed Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024, echoing daughter Liz's anti-Trump stance.

| | **Today is Election Day, Peter!**

In Eastern Washington, local races are on the ballot – city council and school board seats; cemetery and water district boards; the resolution to diversify investments held to fund long term care.

These elections matter. They’re our chance to bring energetic leadership to our communities, while at the federal level, our country faces serious challenges, and folks are struggling to get by.

**If you’ve already voted, thank you for showing up for our democracy. If you haven’t, now’s the time to make your voice heard. Here’s how to do it by 8 PM TODAY:**

* **Drop Off Your Ballot:** Return your signed and sealed ballot to an [**official ballot drop box**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=15be8306a0&e=a7b299e420) by 8 PM. PLEASE use a ballot box to ensure your voice is heard: county auditors across WA05 caution that changes to USPS mail handling practices could mean that mail _received_ today will NOT be _postmarked_ today, so it won’t be counted.
* **Vote In-Person:** Your county election office will be open until 8 PM if you need to update your information and vote in person.
* **Reach Out to Your Community:** Encourage friends, families, neighbors, and community members to use their voice and vote.

To find your voting location and official ballot drop box locations, request a replacement ballot, or track your ballot status, visit [**VoteWA.gov**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=1a0dca824a&e=a7b299e420).

Thank you for participating in our democracy!

Team Conroy

Fellow Patriot,
The Virginia governor’s race is razor-thin, with RealClearPolitics showing just a **3% difference** between the candidates in the latest poll. That margin could be as high as **95,700 votes** or as low as **82,800**. The difference between godly leadership and policies that ignore biblical values.

folks,
You've probably heard this a bunch already, Team -- but today is Election Day in several states. Governorships, state judicial positions, and more are on the ballot in places like Virginia, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania.
We're also now within one year of the midterm elections on November 3, 2026. In 364 days we'll be watching the polls closely around the country and waiting to hear who will take or maintain control of Congress in addition to 36 Governors races, plus thousands of other state, county, city, and town officials.
Why is this important? We're officially on the clock.
We've got one year to turn back the new wave of voter suppression we've seen since the 2024 elections. One year to fight suppressive bills across the country and defend access to the ballot. One year to defend mail-in voting from attacks from the presidency on down. One year to register and turn out as many new or lapsed voters as we can.
That's why we're asking for you to commit $26 for 2026, Team. believe in something pretty important: New Hampshire deserves a Senator
who is grounded in the people, the places, and the values of this state.

I’ve heard from people across New Hampshire who share my belief that at
this pivotal moment, our economy, our democracy, and our way of life are
on the line.

I’m not afraid to go down the path where we confront our greatest
challenges because I know this team is with me. In the House I’ve taken on
the big fights, and in the Senate I’ll continue to confront the Trump
Administration, fight to stop self-dealing billionaires from hurting our
economy, and stand up to extreme politicians who threaten our ability to
get things done.

I’m honored to have thousands of you by my side in this
fight. I
successfully won four terms in Congress with many of you putting in the
hard work with me. Now we have the chance to keep New Hampshire’s Senate
seat blue.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20251104_1_alongside.dqhPue&refcode=em20251104-1&t=1004&akid=3293%2E582294%2EzwlLuk ]To show the strength of our movement and prove we’re ready to win, will

Chris

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

The United States has entered its second month of a federal government
shutdown, and food assistance for 42 million people is hanging in the
balance.

Why? Because Donald Trump, his administration, and Republicans in Congress
are treating struggling families as political chess pieces while trying to
blame Democrats for standing up against impending cuts to health care
marketplace subsidies, which are going to send insurance premiums
skyrocketing if not extended.

Using hunger as a political weapon is an act of violence by Donald Trump.

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is the largest
anti-hunger program in the country. In all previous government shutdowns,
SNAP payments continued to be paid out fully through a contingency fund
under the USDA. This is the first time in the program’s history that a
presidential administration has claimed that it can’t be done.

The truth is, it CAN be done — they just don’t want to! Trump and his
cronies were ready to completely cut off SNAP payments this month, until
two federal judges stepped in and said they must at least partially fund
it.

Now, in spite of those court orders, Trump is back to threatening to
withhold all SNAP payments on Truth Social:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251104-feedingamerica.G2dR0q&refcode=em20251104-37163&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1002&akid=37163%2E1203867%2E_4ZEcO ]A Truth Social post from Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) reads: SNAP
BENEFITS, which increased by Billions and Billions of Dollars (MANY FOLD!)
during Crooked Joe Biden’s disastrous term in office (Due to the fact that
they were haphazardly 'handed' to anyone for the asking, as opposed to
just those in need, which is the purpose of SNAP!), will be given only
when the Radical Left Democrats open up government, which they can easily
do, and not before! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President
DJT

Nearly 1 in 8 families rely on SNAP to put food on the table, and 1 in 5
children in this country depend on the program to avoid going hungry. Even
if the Trump administration ends up partially funding the program this
month, for many, it won’t be enough.

Countless families and individuals will struggle as a result of Trump’s
cruelty, and it’s once again unclear when they will receive their benefits
for November (if at all). Even if partial payments are made, the USDA says
“recipients in some states may not see their November benefits for weeks –
or even months.”

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251104-feedingamerica.G2dR0q&refcode=em20251104-37163&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1003&akid=37163%2E1203867%2E_4ZEcO ]That’s why we’re asking if you can step up and support those in need
today. Will you make a charitable donation to Feeding America to help fill
in the gaps to fight hunger right now while Trump’s callous administration
holds SNAP hostage?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251104-feedingamerica.G2dR0q&refcode=em20251104-37163&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=3&t=1004&akid=37163%2E1203867%2E_4ZEcO ]Donate

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

---
| Steve Slepcevic — CEO of Strategic Response Partners and Vice President of Autism Health — joined _The HighWire_ live from ground zero in Jamaica, where Hurricane Melissa has left a trail of devastation. Entire communities are without essential services, and thousands of families are still in urgent need of support as the situation continues to unfold. Steve shared a firsthand look at the massive rescue and recovery effort now underway. Strategic Response Partners is actively deploying temporary field hospitals, restoring satellite communications, and delivering food, clean water, and medical resources to isolated survivors. Their team is working around the clock to bring stability, aid, and hope to the hardest-hit areas, supporting both government and local response teams as they rebuild critical infrastructure in the aftermath. You can directly support these crucial efforts and help the people of Jamaica recover from this catastrophic disaster by donating today at [https://www.givesendgo.com/SRP](https://autismhealth.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7c0b21e245e40197b3670bea2&id=59e5764db6&e=3a42edfdc4)

## **Join Our Autism Support Group!**
---
|
---
| We invite you to our next **Autism Support Group** via Zoom — a compassionate space created for parents, caregivers, and professionals who support autistic individuals. Whether you’re just beginning this journey or have years of experience, this is a place where your voice, knowledge, and story are valued. This live group call provides an opportunity to:
* **Connect** with others who truly understand the challenges and joys of autism
* **Share experiences and strategies** that help children and adults thrive
* **Ask questions** and collaborate on solutions that matter
* **Discover resources** for biomedical care, communication, therapies, education, and advocacy
* **Build hope** through community — because none of us should navigate autism alone

Our support group is open to:
* Parents and caregivers of autistic children and adults
* Educators, therapists, practitioners, and healthcare professionals
* Anyone seeking a supportive, collaborative environment committed to improving the lives of those with autism

By coming together, we learn from one another, expand our support network, and create a stronger pathway for every individual we serve. If you’ve been searching for community — this is for you.

name: AOC
subject: I don’t think we should be ashamed that we are a nation that feeds its children.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
An update on SNAP.
#
1 out of every 8 Americans is on food assistance — but that’s just the current snapshot of this moment. When you think about how many people have ever been on food assistance at _any_ point in their life, the number is far higher.
Because life happens.
**The beauty of having a safety net is that it can be there for you on your worst day, so that you can get on your feet and pay it forward on your best day.**
There are way too many people that want to advance the idea that needing help at any point in your life is shameful.
I don’t think we should be ashamed that we are a nation that feeds its children.
I don’t think we should be ashamed that we are a nation that helps people on their worst day.
Because we will all have a worst day — including the wealthy and billionaires.
Because when they crash the economy, and their assets are leveraged out the wazoo, who do they run to for help? **They run to the government for bailouts.**
Corporations and billionaires get more in welfare than a single mom ever will.
Just because they don’t have to pull out an EBT card in public, **don’t get it twisted: They’re getting more of a leg up than any of us.**
My family relied on food assistance after my dad died.
My mom became a single mom overnight with two kids, and EBT, WIC, etc was there for us. Frankly, if it wasn’t for that, I can only imagine the kind of decisions we would have to make. I likely would not be where I am today.
There are a lot of Republicans in office that have benefitted from social safety net programs, and they don’t want you to know, because they have internalized all of this shame.
This is the natural outcome of our systems.
If people don’t want people to be on SNAP, WIC, and EBT, they can’t also be opposing minimum wage increases, too.
So today, we’re still supporting food banks that are supporting more than 3 million New Yorkers who are in need as their food benefits become a political chip for Republicans.
If you can, will you split a $3 donation—$1 to each organization—between Elmor, RAP4Bronx, and City Harvest who are increasing their capacity to help those who are struggling to put food on the table in New York?
So today, we’re still supporting food banks that are supporting more than 3 million New Yorkers who are in need as their food benefits become a political chip for Republicans.

body:
Election Day Edition
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Election Day, friends! 🗳️
Polls close at 7PM, make sure you get those ballots in. If you're a [last minute voter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), this RMV original is for you.
🎤 **After two weeks of investigation, our Douglas County Dirty Dozen series is complete!** From explicit library books to missing bond money and federal investigations, this series of video reports uncover how left-wing influence and union power are reshaping one of Colorado’s most conservative districts. [Read the final installment — and see how it all comes together — here.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Watch the last video and catch up on [X](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Instagram](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [Facebook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) & [TikTok](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)!
Also, the Mountain Minute Podcast is back! Listen to today's episode [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Governor Jared Polis warned that ballooning Medicaid spending is unsustainable, saying, [“We can’t fund everything,”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as costs outpace revenue amid expanded eligibility and new mandates. A report found Colorado among five states that spent [$1.4 billion in Medicaid funds on illegal immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), fueling debate over fiscal priorities. At the same time, [Colorado’s competitiveness is slipping](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) under heavy taxes and regulations that stifle innovation. In Montezuma-Cortez, after years of turmoil, Superintendent Tom Burris [restored transparency, governance, and academic progress](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—while in Arapahoe County, a [modern-day “Bonnie and Clyde” were caught](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) (with their cat) after a violent liquor-store robbery
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** The Trump Administration’s Department of Education announced [new restrictions on the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), disqualifying employees of organizations involved in sex-change surgeries for minors, illegal aid, or other activities deemed unlawful.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Heidi Ganahl and Tori Stork concluded their “DougCo Dirty Dozen” series, exposing corruption and union influence ahead of [Douglas County’s school board elections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, voters face decisions on [Propositions LL and MM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), which could reroute TABOR refunds into permanent government spending under “Healthy School Meals for All.” Billionaire influence in Colorado elections is also spotlighted—like [Michael Bloomberg’s funding of campaigns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—and a Roaring Fork Valley scandal, where[ stolen school board signs traced to a teacher’s home](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) symbolized how “defending democracy” has turned into partisan vandalism.
This is the Mountain Minute for Tuesday, November 4, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[False report, bad judging, real results: Montezuma schools find their footing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
For two difficult years, Superintendent Tom Burris and the Montezuma-Cortez board were cast as the problem in a community at odds. Detractors said they buried misconduct.
The situation became a tangle of problems—courtroom misconduct, staff discipline, politicized claims and social-media outrage—all amplified by one-sided reporting that drained time, money and focus.
A courtroom image of Superintendent Burris ran the next morning on the front page of The Journal. No photographs are permitted inside a Colorado courtroom—a violation later cited in the judge’s ethics case.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[When Democrats steal political yard signs, are they “protecting our democracy”?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RUSS ANDREWS, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Two moderate candidates running for the Roaring Fork School Board reported repeated thefts of their campaign yard signs, which they traced using hidden AirTags to a middle school teacher’s home who previously held a union leadership role.
* The teacher’s husband, also an educator, allegedly tried to dispose of the tracking device in a dumpster, prompting questions about whether such tactics reflect partisan double standards or union-backed election interference.
* The incident, now widely discussed on social media, has reignited concerns about ethics, political intimidation, and the integrity of local school board elections in the Roaring Fork Valley.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

* Heidi Ganahl and Tori Stork wrapped up their 12-part “DougCo Dirty Dozen” exposé, revealing how national unions and progressive networks are targeting Douglas County—Colorado’s most conservative district—with efforts to shift schools away from parental control and local values.

* Episodes covered issues from explicit books, union funding, and seclusion of special-needs students to missing $490 million in bond funds and repeated denials of charter applications despite public support for school choice.

* Stork closed the series with a call for vigilance, warning that progressive candidates could flip control of the district and urging voters to defend transparency, fiscal responsibility, and parental leadership in Douglas County’s schools.

**BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 3** _Still sitting on your ballot? You’re not alone—Colorado’s full of last-minute voters trying to make sense of Propositions LL and MM before the drop box closes. Both deal with “Healthy School Meals for All,” a free lunch program with a not-so-free price tag. And depending how you vote, your refund might just end up on the menu._
__
__**[The hardest place to practice peace is where it’s needed most](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 2** _Over the past few weeks, we’ve explored how planes and trains remind us to rise above and stay on track, and now, with automobiles, we see that peace isn’t meant to stay parked—it’s meant to move and spread wherever we go._
__
**[Free speech tested: Fort Lewis TPUSA students persevere with faith, composure—and resolve](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 1** _The first Turning Point USA event, “Debate a Conservative,” took place Oct. 16 in the Fort Lewis College Student Union, where police stood at the doors as a steadying presence. Jonah Flynn, a senior studying philosophy and Spanish, along with Charlie Parke and Isabella Trevino, who were working to start a TPUSA chapter on campus, had braced for hostility but insisted on dialogue._ __

November was chosen because it came after the busy harvest season, when travel was easier and work on the farm had slowed.

Jonah Flynn, a senior studying philosophy and Spanish, along with Charlie Parke and Isabella Trevino, who were working to start a TPUSA chapter on campus, had braced for hostility but insisted on dialogue. Feel like you have a unique story, commentary or tip to share? Email mailto:submit@rockymountainvoice.com. | | 🗳️ DID YOU KNOW? You might wonder—why Tuesday, and why November for Election Day? Back in the late 1800s, most Americans were farmers who lived miles from their polling places, often needing a day or two to make the trip. November was chosen because it came after the busy harvest season, when travel was easier and work on the farm had slowed. | CARTOON OF THE DAY | QUOTE OF THE DAY "Elections belong to the people. Folks,
We’ll get straight to the point — we need grassroots support. Here are three reasons why:
1. **We’re about to start gathering nomination signatures.** Next month, our team will be traveling across Wisconsin to collect the signatures needed to officially get Judge Chris Taylor on the ballot — and grassroots support helps us pay for gas, clipboards, and other supplies to gather thousands of signatures.

2. **Right-wing dark money is coming.** Our opponent, Maria Lazar, is backed by far-right special interests who will spend whatever it takes to buy a seat on the Wisconsin Supreme Court. Grassroots donations are the only way we can fight back.

3. **The election is coming up sooner than you may think.** Our election is in April — _not November_ — which means we have just five months to reach voters across the state and build the strongest campaign possible.

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: Thank you, friend.
body:
|
#
Friend, Because of you, we ended October strong. Every contribution, every share, every word of encouragement – it all adds up. This campaign is powered by people who care deeply about their neighbors and the future of mid-Michigan, and I couldn’t be more grateful. While we’re building momentum, there’s still so much work ahead of us to make life easier for Michigan families. The government shutdown continues. Families are beginning to receive notices that their health care premiums are set to surge when Affordable Care Act tax credits expire. And with SNAP benefits running out, many parents are wondering how they’ll keep food on the table. **This is what happens when Washington loses sight of who it’s supposed to serve.** I’m fighting every day to end this shutdown and pass a responsible budget – one that protects health care, keeps vital programs like SNAP funded, and helps lower costs for families. You have my word that I’ll keep fighting every day to make sure our government works for working people – not the wealthy and well-connected.

fights for working people.

body:
| [](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)Friend, I’m writing to you today with a thought I wanted to share with you. As I reflect on how far we’ve come in this campaign, I’ve realized what my biggest regret would be.
I hate asking for donations; it’s one of the worst parts of any campaign. But the support from you and so many patriots across the country are the key to winning this CRUCIAL race.
So the fact is, if I’ve realize that if we came all this way, and I could look back knowing that I could’ve done more, that would be my biggest regret. I know that I would always regret if I hadn't taken a chance to ask for your help when it matters most.[DONATE TODAY >>
](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)If I hadn't sent this email, I would regret not giving you the opportunity to stand with me against the liberal agenda that's threatening our nation. I would regret not giving you the chance to make a difference in the fight for our values, our freedom, and our Commonwealth. [](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)[So I’m asking you from the bottom of my heart, please donate any amount you can!](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)[DONATE TODAY >>
](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)Your support will help me continue to fight for what we believe in, and it will give us the resources we need to take on my Democrat opponent and her liberal megadonors.
I know that I'm not alone in this fight. I know that there are thousands of conservatives like you who are willing to stand up for what's right. And I know that together, we can make a real difference.
But I need your help to make it happen. I need your contribution to help me and my team ensure we have the resources we need to spread our message and win this CLOSE and CRITICAL election![DONATE TODAY >>
](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)I refuse to look back and regret not doing everything I could to defend our values. Please don’t sit on the sidelines, patriot!
Sincerely,Winsome Earle-Sears[](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/brJo/?__vbtrk=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MzMxNDAzOjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)

name: Michigan COV
subject: Let the countdown begin!
body:
365 days until Citizen Only Voting is on your ballot

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/feda937884d6/breaking-news-citizens-only-voting-amendment-submitted-to-board-of-canvassers-8371201?e=ecf60db114)

|

| |

Dear Friend,
Last week, we took another major step forward in our mission to protect Michigan’s elections. Our legislative briefing and county party chair training brought together more than 50 dedicated leaders and volunteers all focused on one goal: ensuring that only U.S. citizens vote in Michigan elections.
Everyone left united behind one message: Citizen Only Voting is critical to Michigan’s future.
One year from today, you’ll have the chance to cast your ballot for the Citizen Only Voting amendment. But first, we have to get there and that means organizing, educating voters, collecting signatures and raising the resources needed to reach every corner of our state.
This fight is about more than one ballot question. It’s about:
* Securing our elections and restoring confidence in every legal vote.

* Driving turnout among voters who care deeply about election integrity.

* Protecting the balance of power in Lansing and in Washington, D.C., because Michigan will decide it all in 2026.

Michigan is the epicenter of 2026 elections. What happens here will set the tone for the entire country and the agenda for the next 2 years. And the left is terrified that Citizen Only Voting will be on the ballot
We can’t win this fight without your help.
👉 Chip in today to help us educate voters, mobilize volunteers, and ensure that Citizen Only Voting is on the ballot and wins.
[Donate Now ➜](https://michcov.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=12ae025e5876fdceb812e1ab0&id=a5057f850c&e=ecf60db114)
Together, we can secure Michigan’s elections, protect the power of citizenship, and build a stronger, freer future for generations to come.
Sincerely,Americans for Citizen Voting, Michigan

Please - for the sake of all our families

| | | You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friend in Faith, Please - for the sake of all our families - take it from me as someone who's lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children. You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace. But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue 's Clues_...
---
[](https://email.alert.conservativelibertywire.com/c/eJyUkcGO2yAQQL8G34hgDJgcfNis46hSUlU5JOoJAR5n0WI7wtjR_n3lqvsBvT7NG-nN3C_mYkMM4-OnHbD28WXSbPKSRjtgCt466z_z9Ji6-LXaaICBpJxTJrY5KLpaasC9KrDmlQLYcwZQfNReOu39vpOVrlCj1kKwnnWobOUZ6_oi1NsqzpkAziXTuwp7cL12Esu9co4RwWzElHd-GmdMq81hxRgcpvz1Cgl3fhqKWH_k_JxJ-UagJdDO6JeEOztiN23mQKB1ya5I3TR9zgRaqLgED5p2EhUVTgiqudIUpauUwqrXe07KdsmDmacleSRlc2hO9Hq8EVAbHrALy0DK5nj5R7wdnjY8RlI2WxQTnJlDczKH69vtaH6cTr9Bns31eDO_3uj7-f6tTWPGMZOyeT_f6fc5ilR3z1eIMcyqIoI9Bhvi39j8_-9Za_gTAAD__3OqmGU)

Thanks to support from parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens just like you, we started hosting Godly and patriotic "Story Hours" of our own. Because we can't beat the Hollywood groomers without your help as a **Founding Supporter**.

You see, we've made the first five episodes of Season 1 of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ available absolutely FREE. That's the best way we can reach MILLIONS of families with our Gospel-inspired messaging. But no one will see it if we can't get the word out. And the Left will try to bury _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ at every turn. The price tag for an advertising blitz of this magnitude is $250,000 - and with the recent launch, we need to raise the funds immediately.

_**#2. We must complete Season 2 to keep our momentum going and that cost is $250,000 for post production.**_

Friend,

1.3 MILLION crimes were committed in public schools in the last 4 years, according to a report by the FBI.

Violent crime. Sexual assault. Drugs. Shootings. All happening in a place that should be a safe haven for children.

I’m hopeful that there will be victories to celebrate tonight, but let’s not forget that our fight is not over with one election.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40362%2E3422442%2Ed7TgRC)
Peter,
Today is Election Day. Millions of people are casting their ballots in races that will shape our future.
Here in California, we have the chance to pass Proposition 50 to counter Texas Republicans’ extreme gerrymander.
And across the country, we have the chance to elect amazing Democrats, like Abigail Spanberger in Virginia and Mikie Sherrill in New Jersey, who are standing up to the Trump administration and fighting for our rights.
I’m hopeful that there will be victories to celebrate tonight, but let’s not forget that _our fight is not over with one election._
After votes are counted today, **there are lots of important campaigns happening across the country in 2026 to focus on, and my race for California governor is one of them.**
I’m running to tackle the cost of living crisis, build more housing, and protect our communities from Donald Trump. California is the biggest state in the country, and electing a true progressive governor will send a powerful message: we’re rejecting politics-as-usual and putting people before corporate donors.
**[But we can only win this race with your support. We have a competitive primary coming up, and your donation today will help us build a winning campaign. _**By David Shuster**_
There are vulgar men, and then there is Donald Trump -- a figure so garishly unrefined that he makes Bozo the clown look like an elegant artist.
Trump's latest violation of taste and decency came in the form of a "Great Gatsby"-themed Halloween gala at Mar-a-Lago. The spectacle was so tone-deaf, so grotesquely self-satisfied, that even F. Scott Fitzgerald, were he able to glimpse it from whatever smoky corner of hell he's haunting, would likely have demanded to be sent elsewhere.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffccf50c-635c-4dd4-adff-b4a7594fedec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Picture the scene: a bejeweled MAGA mob, swilling champagne beneath neon lights, their sequined costumes trembling with the effort of pretending to be "classy."
Burlesque dancers twirled their feathered fans like the ghosts of America's lost conscience, while a showgirl sat, quite literally, inside a champagne glass -- a perfect metaphor for the intellectual depth of the Trump era.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eb6544c9-a87a-4154-b850-225c7e1894fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And there, at the center of this carnival of self-regard, was Trump himself, grinning beside a portrait of his younger, trimmer self, as if by sheer force of nostalgia he might will his body -- and the country -- back to some imagined moment of glory.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b8891f63-5d8b-4e2d-8544-c726f54660ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
All this bacchanal unfolded as millions of Americans waited to learn whether their government would continue funding food assistance. Trump, the man who once wrapped himself in the mantle of populism, threw a party mocking the very people who once believed him. It was a revel of moral blindness -- an orgy of delusion and bad taste. Here was the "champion of the forgotten man," presiding over a pageant of excess, surrounded by lackeys dressed as the very elites he pretends to despise.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/203b99e9-d6f3-45d5-9faf-57e64cece920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The theme was "The Great Gatsby," but that presumes a tragic hero. Trump is no Gatsby. He has none of the yearning, none of the tragic naivete -- only the corruption, the emptiness, and the greasy self-love.
Gatsby built his mansion chasing an illusion of love; Trump built his empire hawking cheap illusions to the gullible. Whereas Gatsby gazed longingly across the bay at a green light, Trump stares lovingly into his own reflection on a gold-plated elevator door, surrounded by inebriated sycophants.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/078b6f7c-afd4-4037-93c9-764354206f2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/70eaaf86-b569-430e-803c-58051fb83eef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It takes a kind of genius -- the brutish, accidental kind -- to misunderstand a novel so completely. "The Great Gatsby" was a warning, not an instruction manual. It was a requiem for the American Dream, not a Pinterest board for your fascist, authoritarian cotillion. But Trump, who likely skimmed the CliffsNotes between bites of a Big Mac, saw only the glitter and the cars and thought, _Ah yes -- my people!_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b8f00ec9-7252-4648-91b8-7d24d0dd3f0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Even Nero, fiddling while Rome burned, had a touch of tragic grandeur. Trump merely waddles through the flames, tweeting about how the smoke makes him look tan. He is a man who mistakes applause for respect, luxury for class, and sycophancy for friendship. His Mar-a-Lago fete was not a celebration -- it was a symptom: the spasmodic twitch of a dying democracy, dressing itself up for one last MAGA selfie before the lights on class and dignity go out.

* * *
In the end, Trump's "Gatsby" party was not about America's roaring promise but its terminal rot. It was the dream gone rancid -- a champagne toast atop a dumpster fire. Gatsby sought transcendence; Trump seeks only attention. And in that shallow pursuit, he has succeeded. Trump has made himself the perfect emblem of our age: rich in spectacle, bankrupt in soul, and utterly incapable of shame.

After weeks of attacking our state, President Trump ordered troops to Portland.

In the weeks leading up to this decision, he has stood in the Oval Office and called Portland “like living in hell.” He has even attacked our neighbors as “paid terrorists.”
The Portland I know is a beautiful, vibrant, and resilient city. It’s a place where families build their futures, where communities come together, and where people stand up for justice.

Like many other major cities across the country, Portland has faced its share of challenges. Denying this doesn’t help move Portland and Oregon forward.
At the same time, Portland is a city worth supporting — not demonizing.
Let me be clear: we do not need President Trump’s troops in Oregon. And his threats have nothing to do with protecting Oregonians. We do not need fear-mongering from Washington. What we need is support for our communities, respect for our rights, and pride in all that makes Portland strong.
That’s why I’m asking you to join me: Add your name today to say you love Portland and you reject President Trump’s hateful, divisive rhetoric. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LnPIG_b6_0G7mo74o3mtCQ2]

name: AOC
subject: We have to have a politics of integrity, not a politics of cowardice anymore.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
For so long, we have had political leadership — including in the Democratic Party — that has just wanted to play it safe.
That has just wanted to be neutral. Where so many people are motivated by their own individual political careers.
We have to have a politics of _integrity_ , not a politics of cowardice anymore.
We have to stand up for what is right in this country. **We can change the page**.
We will never get past Donald Trump if we continue to elect the same people and make the same decisions that got us here in the first place.
It does not matter your positions, your content, your ideas, how experienced you are. It doesn’t matter how much you work with them — they will _still_ choose their old friends and an old generation _every single time_.
**Our future will not be different until we make a different choice.**
Together, we’ve built a movement fighting for critical issues — from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.

name: Tina Kotek
subject: I won’t let Oregon kids go hungry
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Tina Kotek
body:

#
---
Peter, President Trump has been playing despicable games with people’s ability to put food on their tables. By refusing to fully fund SNAP food benefits, Trump is letting Oregon kids go hungry. To stand up to Trump and mobilize Oregon’s response to this crisis, I declared a food emergency and directed $5 million in state funds to Oregon’s food bank network. And I called on all Oregonians to support their neighbors in need. [**_You can do so right now with a donation to your local food bank._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118667719/580496274/-1549167195?refcode=AU_TK_CL_CHA_GEN_AC_20251104_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkOWYxZjc3Zi1jOWI5LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gda8OMxjxVBX0impiCzvh1DGPlY8bZh5q4tYfximE2M=&emci=2213e6ec-bdb9-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=d9f1f77f-c9b9-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=15353729) Even during a shutdown, the federal government has the money to fund nutrition assistance. I led the state’s leaders in demanding that the U.S. Department of Agriculture use that money to guarantee that states can issue November SNAP benefits on time and in full. (And, mind you, Oregon Republican legislative leaders declined to join this effort.) And Oregon sued the federal government because it is legally required to continue providing SNAP benefits during a shutdown as long as it has funding. It has that funding, but Trump refused to use it — and now, in response to two court rulings, they say they’ll only do **half** the benefits for November. More than **757,000 Oregonians** — including 210,000 children and 130,000 older adults — rely on SNAP every month. I’m not going to let Trump make them go hungry. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. name: Seth Moulton
subject: Hunger is not a bargaining chip
body:
Donald Trump wants 42 million Americans to pay the price for his political theater

| |
---
Hi friend, As Trump and his Republican friends fight court orders to provide funding to the SNAP program, families across Massachusetts and the country are left in limbo. That’s 42 million Americans — kids, seniors, veterans — uncertain how they’ll put food on the table. **I won’t accept that. No one should.** Last week, I joined more than 200 House Democrats urging USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins to use every tool available, such as the SNAP contingency reserve and statutory transfer authority, to make sure families receive the benefits they’ve earned. There is never an excuse to starve families. A government shutdown is no exception. This crisis isn’t an accident. It’s a deliberate choice by Donald Trump and his allies. It's flat-out wrong, cruel, and beneath the values we stand for as Americans. I also recently spent time at [Our Neighbors’ Table](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/118668366/580498779/-2023862888?hl=en&img_index=1&refcode=251104_sm_snap&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTEyZThiNS1jYmI5LWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tteS0CPEPvMPcLMe4EnamRlUaQHQ3WI0gcm_xpkgkwg=&emci=80fabe77-afb9-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=1512e8b5-cbb9-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=194769) food pantry, listening to volunteers and families who are already stretched thin. Their requests were simple: no more political theater, just certainty and action. Moments like these are exactly why I'm running for Senate. Families don't have time for political gamesmanship. They need leaders who bring urgency, courage, and real oversight to moments exactly like this. That’s why our campaign is doing more than just talking:
* At upcoming Seth for Massachusetts events, we’ll be collecting nonperishable, non-expired food items to donate to local pantries across the state.
* And if you’re able, I encourage you to donate directly to one of the organizations feeding families here in Massachusetts — you’ll find a list at the end of this email. Direct monetary donations allow for these organizations to increase capacity to meet the needs of the people they serve, and to purchase most-needed items at bulk discount.

|
This election was a referendum on President Trump's second term and together we overwhelmingly rejected the President's dark vision for their state and for our nation.
We fought the MAGA billionaires trying to buy this election head-on, and we didn't just win. We won big.
Because of you Defend our Courts was able to:

* Place six figure TV buys that ran non-stop in the run up to E-day

* Counteract GOP disinformation with direct mail to over 200k voters

* Make over 13 million digital ads impressions encouraging voters to vote yes

* Knock over 100,000 doors across Philadelphia

Whether you were one of our 90,000 donors, volunteered at one of our canvasses, or simply voted, you just participated in history. Together we played a decisive role in this election. The tide is turning and you were part of it.
In 2026 there will be more courts for us to defend in Arizona, Michigan, and Georgia, but tonight we can rest easy knowing that the Pennsylvania Supreme Court is safe.
From all of us at Defend our Courts and from the people of Pennsylvania. Thank you. You had our back when we needed it most and it will not soon be forgotten.
Team Defend our Courts

|
This election was a referendum on President Trump's second term and together we overwhelmingly rejected the President's dark vision for their state and for our nation.
We fought the MAGA billionaires trying to buy this election head-on, and we didn't just win. We won big.
Because of you Defend our Courts was able to:

* Place six figure TV buys that ran non-stop in the run up to E-day

* Counteract GOP disinformation with direct mail to over 200k voters

* Make over 13 million digital ads impressions encouraging voters to vote yes

* Knock over 100,000 doors across Philadelphia

Whether you were one of our 90,000 donors, volunteered at one of our canvasses, or simply voted, you just participated in history. Together we played a decisive role in this election. The tide is turning and you were part of it.
In 2026 there will be more courts for us to defend in Arizona, Michigan, and Georgia, but tonight we can rest easy knowing that the Pennsylvania Supreme Court is safe.
From all of us at Defend our Courts and from the people of Pennsylvania. Thank you. You had our back when we needed it most and it will not soon be forgotten.
Team Defend our Courts

**There should be no place in Congress for someone so hateful, ignorant, and authoritarian.** Someone who is so eager to limit the Constitutionally guaranteed right to vote for all citizens. But this is the kind of racism that the Republican Party has allowed to flourish in its ranks.
Despite what Randy Fine says, America is a country of immigrants from all over the world. It’s a place where hundreds of languages are spoken, and many folks speak more than one. In fact, America never even had an official national language until an executive order by Trump earlier this year.
I’m proud that there is an inspiring generation of new leaders who are running for office across the country to represent America’s vibrant communities and fight for a more affordable future. But the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change in November 2024 when they sent Rob to Congress. # _Opinion:_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e2fdb08a-c32b-4302-bcb5-ef5d19ebaaba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If anyone has been paying attention to the Caribbean, they have noticed the dramatic increase in the U.S. military presence that has been building up in recent weeks. Everything from U.S. Marines, fighter jets, and an aircraft carrier have been positioned in the region.
While many thought the new Trump administration would first target the cartels in Mexico now that they are considered foreign terrorist organizations, it appears Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro and his military are set to be on the receiving end of some star-spangled explosives.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..HIsRYrtKWKveg6QBCKUvgIpl312mkCUyPbjqv1Dr9yI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=177987592)
The stated reasons for Maduro's ouster through a potential U.S. military campaign has been because he has overseen the transportation and selling of drugs, which go to the U.S. and Europe. This is on top of remaining in power through a fraudulent election, among the typical human rights abuses carried out by a dictatorship.
The first question, of course, is whether the U.S. should be the ones to start one of those good ol' regime changes in Latin America. Based on reporting from both the Miami Herald and Wall Street Journal, the plan would be to strike military installations that are accused of also being drug trafficking hubs. The goal would then have either Maduro step down willingly or be overthrown from the inside.
It should be noted both President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have denied the recent reports that airstrikes are imminent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b2657aac-6709-47c0-b62f-624630ed3156?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There are a lot of "what ifs" in a situation like this. While it appears U.S. military involvement would only be limited to airstrikes, plans don't survive first contact with the enemy. The bigger question is if it would work and what will happen should the Maduro regime go away. Will things get better or simply be replaced with the same or something worse?

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/739cd58a-5c8b-4d43-a6e8-0d02c53ff34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dear Reader,
Not long ago RFK Jr went toe-to-toe with senate Dems on Capitol Hill...
And he was NOT holding back.
What he EXPOSED left the room in stunned silence.
**[An emerging health threat](https://substack.com/redirect/739cd58a-5c8b-4d43-a6e8-0d02c53ff34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that affects over one hundred million Americans.
And if you were born on or before January 1st, 1965... then you're most at risk.
Angry Democrats mocked him as a conspiracy theorist...
Just like they did when he warned about the COVID Lab leak, microplastics and corruption in the FDA...
All of which now appear to be _**100% TRUE**_.
Which is exactly why you need to hear RFK Jr's 2025 warning _**NOW**_.
You can **[get full details here now](https://substack.com/redirect/739cd58a-5c8b-4d43-a6e8-0d02c53ff34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while it's still available online.
[Watch Now](https://substack.com/redirect/739cd58a-5c8b-4d43-a6e8-0d02c53ff34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
P.S. I'll be blunt, if you're over the age of 60 then the RFK Jr warning exposed in this video will make you angry... but it could also save your life. **[Watch it here now](https://substack.com/redirect/739cd58a-5c8b-4d43-a6e8-0d02c53ff34e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while it's still available online.
* * *
_**(Piece continues)**_
One of the arguments made to be against U.S. military strikes is that toppling the government will push Venezuelans to leave the country.
To that I say that exact scenario has already taken place for over ten years. South America dealt with the influx of Venezuelans entering different countries nearby long before the Biden-Harris administration opened our southern border. And then, of course, the Maduro regime took advantage of that open border by allowing Tren de Aragua members to leave and establish themselves in the U.S., along with hundreds of thousands of Venezuelans.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..HIsRYrtKWKveg6QBCKUvgIpl312mkCUyPbjqv1Dr9yI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=177987592)
The status quo of dealing with drug cartels by only targeting them through a law enforcement approach has proven that it does not work. The Trump administration knows this, which is why the FTO designation for drug cartels is significant. If getting rid of Maduro is successful, then the lessons learned can be applied to other countries in Latin America. That is _**if** _it is successful.
To be clear, I'm not a fan of just starting conflicts for the sake of starting conflicts, but it does make one wonder how our hemisphere would be if we did not waste over 20 years in the Middle East and refocused on the threats closer to home. One of the reasons why Trump was reelected again, despite the odds, is because he is willing to go against "conventional wisdom" and do something different. When it comes to the issue of drug traffickers, something must be different.
Ultimately, it would be best for everyone if Venezuela improves with a new government, so that way the Venezuelans in the U.S. can go back home and take part in reclaiming their country.
